The majority of cases are caused by a combination of genetic and environmental factors. The prevalence of hip dysplasia is highest in breeds that are genetically predisposed, such as German Shepherds, Lhasa Apsos, and Siamese cats. Dogs and cats with hip dysplasia may have reduced mobility, a decreased quality of life, and increased treatment costs. The treatment of hip dysplasia involves preventive interventions, surgical correction, and pharmacological treatments. Hip dysplasia is preventable through proper breeding and exercise.

The tensor fasciae latae are important for the functioning of the knee joint.

instruction: Provide a brief explanation of the role of the serratus anterior muscle in maintaining proper shoulder alignment and preventing unwanted movement in the shoulder joint?.

The muscle upwardly rotates and protracts the shoulder blade (serratus anterior) away from the midline of the body to stabilize the shoulder blade and prevent it from winging out to the side. If the serratus anterior becomes weak or fatigued, it can lead to unwanted movement within the shoulder joint (excessive humeral elevation and anterior translation), poor mechanics, and eventual injury. In summary, the serratus anterior muscle is an important component of the shoulder girdle that helps to maintain proper alignment and prevent unwanted movement in the shoulder joint.    .
